Gross margin improved to 61%, from 58% a year earlier, mainly because subscriptions carry higher margins than hardware. Operating income was $14 million, compared with $9 million in the prior-year quarter.

## Regional performance

Revenue in North America grew 6% to $51 million. Europe grew 8% to $27 million, and Asia-Pacific was the fastest-growing region, up 14% to $17 million. The company opened a sales office in Singapore in April to support Asia-Pacific customers.

Northwind ended the quarter with $310 million in cash and short-term investments and no outstanding debt. During the quarter the company repurchased $20 million of its shares. The board did not change the quarterly dividend, which remains $0.40 per share.

## People

Headcount was 2,150 at the end of June, up from 1,980 a year earlier. Most of the new hires joined the engineering and customer success teams.

question: What benefits do employees get?

retrieval.preview: # Northwind Systems — Employee Benefits Policy (2026)
retrieval.content:
# Northwind Systems — Employee Benefits Policy (2026)

*Fictional sample document for the VERITAS demo.*

## Parental leave

Employees receive 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave after the birth or adoption of a child. Leave can be taken in one block or in up to three separate periods, as long as all of it is used within the first year. Employees on parental leave keep their full health coverage.

## Learning stipend

Full-time employees are eligible for an annual learning stipend of $1,000 for courses, certifications, books and conference tickets. Part-time employees receive a prorated stipend based on their contracted hours. Unused stipend does not carry over to the next calendar year.

## Hybrid work

Most roles follow a hybrid schedule with two or three office days per week, agreed with the employee's manager. Fully remote arrangements require approval from a department head and are reviewed every twelve months.

## Retirement plan

The company matches employee retirement contributions dollar for dollar up to 4% of base salary. Matching contributions vest immediately.

## Travel

All international business travel requires pre-approval from the employee's manager and the finance team at least two weeks before departure. Domestic trips under $1,500 only need manager approval.

## Overview

Atlas is Northwind's analytics suite for operations teams. It combines dashboards, scheduled reports and anomaly alerts on top of a customer's existing data warehouse, without copying the data into a separate system.

## Availability

A public beta opened in May 2026 with 140 participating customers. General availability is planned for the third quarter of 2026. Atlas will be offered in two tiers: Team, at $49 per user per month, and Enterprise, priced by contract.

## Features

- Dashboards that refresh every five minutes, or in real time on the Enterprise tier.
- Anomaly alerts that compare each metric with its typical weekly pattern and notify users by email or chat.
- Scheduled PDF reports delivered daily, weekly or monthly.
- Role-based access control and single sign-on on both tiers; audit logs on the Enterprise tier only.

## Security and compliance

Atlas runs in Northwind's existing data centers in Virginia and Oregon. A third data center, in Dublin, Ireland, is scheduled to go live in 2027 for customers who need their data stored in the European Union. Northwind's platform is certified to ISO 27001 and completed its first SOC 2 Type II audit in 2025.

## Beta results

Beta customers reported that Atlas cut the time spent preparing weekly operations reports from about six hours to under one hour. The beta did not measure the effect on decision quality.
